According to the text:

- After 1500 cycles at 1C, the cathode delivers 306 mAh/gS per gram of sulfur (Figure 2E).
- The cathode delivers 87 mAh/g after 1500 cycles at 100% depth of discharge (DOD), which is the whole electrode mass (sulfur, microporous carbon, binder, carbon black, and ideal sodium anode).
- The sulfur content in the electrode is 35 wt%.

To find the sulfur share of the electrode, we can calculate the ratio of the capacity delivered per gram of sulfur to the capacity delivered per gram of the whole electrode:

306 mAh/gS / 87 mAh/g ≈ 3.52

This ratio implies that the sulfur share of the electrode is approximately 3.52 times the sulfur content stated in the paper (35 wt%). Therefore, the sulfur share of the electrode is approximately 122.2 wt% (3.52 × 35 wt%).

However, this calculation does not make sense, as the sulfur share of the electrode cannot be more than 100%. This discrepancy may be due to the fact that the calculation is based on the capacity delivered per gram of sulfur and per gram of the whole electrode, which may not accurately represent the sulfur content of the electrode.
